scope: Independent read-only source and safety review of v0.2.22 relative-runner shutdown repair; no candidate source edits.

resolved_before_final_review.detail: The final hash includes the ^[a-z]: alternative, so C:native_runner.js remains a relative runner instead of being mistaken for a different script.

verified_invariants: The original absolute-workspace command occurrence guard executes before actual-script parsing.
Simple parsing fully consumes the command; unsupported, unbalanced, mixed, escaped-closing-quote, control-character, executable-mismatch, or unsupported-option forms use the old broad matcher.

Actual-script classification recognizes the exact native_runner.js basename, including drive-relative C:native_runner.js; later script arguments are not mistaken for the directly executed script when parsing succeeds.
Every included non-ancestor original row is strictly preflighted before any exact disappearance query; an already readable current-workspace worker cannot be retired by a later absence.
Relative rows retain exact PID, full CreationDate, executable name, parent PID, and known command binding. Command mutation and identity mutation fail conservatively.
Unreadable-to-relative transitions remain pending and bind the first readable command instead of being marked resolved.
Relative ambiguity can resolve only by exact successfully enumerated absence; persistent ambiguity retains the lock.
After relative absence and clearance of the first retained inventory, exactly one fresh complete inventory is required before success.
The post-exit complete inventory rejects a new relative ambiguity immediately; it does not initiate a second relative-host waiting phase.
The post-exit inventory rejects reappearance or contradictory identity of an already checked absent PID and compares bound relative commands.
Sealed own-launch and exact owner-generation/self-identity guards execute before and after every inventory iteration, including the post-exit iteration.
Fresh admitted-host and read-only-follower exceptions remain byte-identical; there is no new parent/PID/name allowlist or foreign-workspace inference.
Acquisition and stale-recovery function bodies remain byte-identical and receive no shutdown retry mechanism; their common guard receives the deliberate actual-script classification correction.
Failure is caught by the unchanged parallelShutdown path, which marks shutdown unclean; the unchanged main cleanup releases the lock only when shutdown is clean.
Compiler, cache key, anchor reuse, axiom audit, memory policy, and mathematical status function bodies remain byte-identical.

static_bounds_per_shutdown_call.bound_note: The second complete inventory may run in the same outer attempt. It adds two owner/self guard queries, so the self-query bound is 14 rather than 12. Rows re-queued in the final inventory consume the same cumulative 64-row budget.

remaining_limits: This is a conservative WMI snapshot and ownership guard, not an atomic operating-system process-tree containment guarantee.
WMI query wall-clock duration is not hard-bounded by the retry/sleep budgets.
Unsupported command syntax retains the old broad matcher and can still produce conservative false positives.
A persistent ambiguous host, a newly ambiguous host in the final inventory, an identity contradiction, or an exhausted budget intentionally retains the lock.
The review does not establish which process caused the original user failure; the old log omitted the offending identity and command shape.
verification_performed: Manual unchanged shutdown-failure and release-path review
verification_not_performed: No candidate JavaScript execution by this reviewer
No native Windows or WSH execution
regression_status: Separate implementation-bound Node-VM mock suite is owned by /root/regression_review; no mock result is claimed by this review.
